session_read: Sunday 19:04 ET. Nothing traded, nothing was published, and the book is identical to yesterday's to the cent. The only new fact in the world is that futures reopened green -- ES +0.07%, NQ +0.22% -- and TWO agents searched independently for a reason and neither found one. An unexplained 0.2% futures tick is not a signal, and the gate flipping AMBIGUOUS to STABILIZING on it changes nothing. So the honest output is that no new proposal is warranted, and the twelve already open are unchanged: eight trims against $12.25 of cash, ten names over their ATR caps, 88.99% single-factor, into NVDA's print on 08-26 at 7.72% weight. What IS new comes from smith-tax's first dispatch in the desk's history. It settles the LTCG question outright -- the earliest open lot is 2026-07-15, so nothing crosses the 24-month boundary until 2028, and every trim on the list is short-term. Where it earns its keep is smaller and real: specifying HIFO rather than letting FIFO run saves $107 of realised gain on MU and NBIS, and it says plainly that the other six trims differ by ten dollars and are not worth complicating. It also declined to recommend harvesting $283 of losses across thirteen names, five of which it holds a strengthening thesis on -- selling conviction for a sub-fifty-dollar offset. The desk's own record stands at seven graded proposals and 14.3%, which is a small sample and not a flattering one.
